newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO, U.S. security talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO, U.S. security talks.

text.p: Israeli, Palestinian and U.S. security officials met the West Bank Palestinian enclave of Ramallah on Sunday as part of a framework set by U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross, Israeli security sources said.
The talks, which were closed to the media, ended just before midnight local time (2100 GMT). Palestinian officials were not immediately available for comment.

But the Israeli sources said the Palestinians gave them results of checks made on explosives found in early July a West Bank apartment suspected of being a bomb laboratory of the anti-Israeli Hamas movement.
The Israelis expressed satisfaction at the information, which they said needed to be checked against data which they already had.

A leaflet in Hamas's name claimed responsibility for a July 30 double suicide bombing at a Jerusalem market. Israeli and Palestinian officials have questioned the authenticity of the claim and the two bombers, who killed 14 other people, have yet to be identified.
The bombing complicated efforts to break a deadlock in Israeli-Palestinian peace talks, which stalled after Israel began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused the Palestinian Authority of not doing enough to fight anti-Israeli guerrillas in its territory.
Ross spent four days in the region last week to arrange the Israeli-Palestinian security talks which were also attended by U.S. representatives.

He also prepared the ground for a visit to the Middle East planned for September by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright. She has demanded improved Israeli-Palestinian security cooperation before she makes her maiden trip to the region.

Britain's Sunday Telegraph newspaper said Israel's Shin Bet secret police chief Ami Ayalon was in London to investigate claims the Jerusalem suicide bombing was carried out by Arab guerrillas based in Britain. A spokesman said Netanyahu's office was checking the report.
The militant Hamas and Islamic Jihad movements have killed scores of Israelis in their violent campaign to sabotage interim peace deals between Israel and the Palestinians.

Israeli government sources said Netanyahu sent an envoy to thank Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for quickly arresting the Palestinian killers of an Israeli taxi driver at the weekend. The men were car thieves.

They said the envoy, Yitzhak Molho, secretly met Arafat in Gaza on Saturday night in a sign of a slight easing of tensions between the sides. They said the men also discussed Ross's visit and sanctions Israel imposed on Palestinians after the bombing.

Israel, which has sealed off Palestinian areas and frozen millions of dollars of financial transfers owed to the Palestinian Authority, says Arafat must arrest militants and crush the infrastructure of Islamist groups before it will lift the sanctions.
The Palestinians say the measures are collective punishment and Washington has condemned them as counterproductive and unhelpful.
Arafat rejected Israeli allegations that his planned "national unity" talks with militant Palestinian groups set for this week amounted to "appeasement of terrorism."
"No doubt we are against terrorist activities...but this is a Palestinian interest and we are insisting on carrying on dialogue with all Palestinian groups," Arafat told reporters in Gaza.
"We are as Palestinians completely committed to the peace process and at the same time we are facing collective punishment from the Israeli government."
